Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light-check search surfaced clearly authoritative, corroborating sources, so this row was moved from the fast path to the full path. Data Protection Africa's Liberia fact sheet (updated 28 January 2026) states plainly 'no data protection law' exists. DLA Piper's Data Protection Laws of the World (last modified February 2024) confirms the same. A draft bill, 'An Act for the Collection, Processing, Transmission, Storage, Protection, and Use of Personal Information in Liberia', was submitted by President Boakai and referred to the House Committee on Post and Telecommunications in June 2025, but remained unenacted as of the January 2026 fact-sheet update. The original score of 0/Unknown was therefore incorrect; recalculated to 1=No on the 0=Unknown/1=No/2=Yes scale, since no legislation is yet in force.
revised_comments: Liberia has no comprehensive data protection law in force. A draft Personal Data Protection and Privacy Bill, submitted to the Legislature by President Boakai and referred to the House Committee on Post and Telecommunications in June 2025, remains under committee review and has not been enacted. In the interim, data privacy is addressed only fragmentarily through Article 16 of the Constitution (right to privacy) and the 2002 Electronic Transactions Law, neither of which constitutes dedicated data protection legislation covering personal data linked to the ID system.

revision_notes: A light-check search surfaced clearly authoritative, corroborating sources, so this row was moved from the fast path to the full path. DLA Piper's Data Protection Laws of the World states 'No specific national data protection agency or authority exists in Liberia'. Data Protection Africa's Liberia fact sheet (updated 28 January 2026) confirms 'Data Protection Authority not appointed'. DataGuidance corroborates: 'Liberia has not established a data protection authority.' Liberia is a signatory to the ECOWAS Supplementary Act requiring member states to establish a national data authority but has not yet done so; the draft Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2024 would extend the Independent Information Commission's mandate to cover this role, but it remains unenacted. The original score of 0/Unknown was therefore incorrect; recalculated to 1=No on the 0=Unknown/1=No/2=Yes scale.
revised_comments: Liberia has no dedicated Data Protection Authority regulating personal data collection and sharing, including by the ID system. The Liberia Telecommunications Authority regulates telecoms data flows and cybersecurity standards but does not function as a general data protection regulator. Liberia is a signatory to the ECOWAS Supplementary Act on Personal Data Protection, which requires member states to establish a national data authority, but has not yet done so. A draft Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act would extend the mandate of the Independent Information Commission to cover data protection oversight, but this remains unenacted.
